question: Can correction infrastructure change permission to assert a proposition when the speaker's evidence, confidence, content and audience are fixed?

terms.evidence_level_propriety: Whether the speaker's evidence meets the relevant epistemic standard for categorical assertion of p.
terms.communicative_permission: Whether the speaker may perform the whole message act, considering foreseeable consequences, alternatives and duties.
terms.practice_level_record_permission: Whether an assertion and its correction obligations may be entered into a shared, updateable record; its epistemic status remains to be defended.

claim.revised: Correction availability alone does not improve evidence-level entitlement to assert p. It can change all-things-considered permission and may affect a separately defended practice-level record norm.
claim.relation_to_original: Narrows the original idea. The strong reading that repairability makes an otherwise unsupported categorical assertion epistemically proper is rejected unless a separate record-level norm is established.

premises.text: Hold fixed the speaker's evidence, confidence, proposition, categorical force, audience and information about p at assertion time.
A correction channel by itself adds no evidence that p is true and changes neither p nor the speaker's knowledge or justification concerning p.
If evidence-level propriety depends on the speaker's evidential relation to p and the applicable assertion standard, P1 and P2 leave that propriety unchanged.
All-things-considered permission may depend on foreseeable uptake, repair costs, alternatives and obligations, which a reliable correction channel can change.
An updateable public-record practice may impose duties of monitoring and visible correction, but its classification as epistemic rather than practical or moral requires an independent defense.

inferences.text: If the evidence standard is fixed, a channel change without an evidence change cannot raise the speaker's evidence-level entitlement.
Repairability can change all-things-considered permission by changing the communication act's foreseeable lifecycle.
Practice-level permission may vary with the right and duty to correct, but this is not established as an epistemic entitlement.

conclusions.text: Repairability alone cannot establish evidence-level permission to make a bare categorical assertion that fails the relevant evidence standard.
Repairability can affect all-things-considered communicative permission.
A distinct practice-level epistemic permission is possible only if an updateable-record norm is independently defended and survives cost-matched tests.

worked_case.proposition: The east archive room is open.
worked_case.fixed: Same incomplete but credible report, confidence, sentence, audience, initial uptake and information about the proposition.
worked_case.contrast: One speaker can append a visible correction and is answerable for doing so; the other cannot edit the assertion, while a moderator sends an equally visible correction at the same time.
worked_case.controlled_outcomes: Stipulate equal initial uptake, final belief, reliance, delay and practical cost.
worked_case.diagnostic: A residual permission difference may indicate accountability or record governance; it is not yet evidence of changed warrant. No residual difference supports a consequences-based narrowing.

objections.challenge: A knowledge norm makes an unknowing categorical assertion epistemically impermissible regardless of correction capacity.
objections.reply: Concede for evidence-level propriety unless the knowledge norm is separately challenged; investigate only separate considered or practice-level permission.

objections.challenge: Correction only reduces expected harm above an unchanged epistemic floor.
objections.reply: Concede as the default explanation; use a cost-matched case. A residual difference identifies an accountability norm, not automatically an epistemic one.

objections.challenge: A correction duty changes the speech act, so the asserted content or force is not held fixed.
objections.reply: If the public undertaking changes meaning, report a different communicative package, not different warrant for the same bare assertion.

disconfirmation_conditions: Permission judgments do not vary after evidence, audience evidence, uptake, final beliefs, delays and costs are controlled.
The effect disappears once correction availability cannot serve as evidence about p.
The record-level account cannot be distinguished from practical loss, moral accountability or changed utterance meaning.
A stable evidence norm fixes the relevant threshold and correction changes none of its conditions.
Nominally available but ineffective correction still appears to raise permission.
literature_status: No sources retrieved or read; closest-source and originality questions remain open.
